passage:
Honestly, it was scary how well it worked. In our group Jomon decided every week who was in. On Monday it was Kabir, who got the front seat, the jokes, the extra dessert. By Thursday Kabir was out and everyone stopped replying to him in the chat. Nobody said why. We just knew.

I'm Farhan, and I stayed quiet because I didn't want to be next. The thing is, Jomon didn't shout. He just went a bit cold and looked at you a little too long. People started agreeing with everything he said. I watched Kabir laugh too hard at every joke, trying to come back in. I remember thinking Jomon looked tired, not powerful.

qa.q: Who decided every week who was in the group?
qa.a: Jomon decided every week who was in the group.

qa.q: Why did Farhan stay quiet?
qa.a: Farhan was afraid of being next, and the fear of losing standing kept Farhan silent.

qa.q: What could Farhan try to loosen the fear in the group?
qa.a: Farhan could check in with Kabir privately and sit with Kabir, showing that friendship does not have to depend on Jomon's mood.

qa.q: What might Jomon be feeling, looking tired rather than powerful?
qa.a: Jomon may feel pressure to keep control and worry that anyone could leave, so the coldness may hide anxiety.

grounding: A peer watches the group's leader decide who is in favour each week, keeping members anxious and obedient.

passage:
I'm Vaibhav, and I sat near Tenzin's table at lunch for a whole term. Tenzin decided who mattered. One week it was Ria: she got the seat next to Tenzin, her jokes were repeated, everyone tagged her. The next week Tenzin stopped looking at Ria at all. Ria kept asking, “What did I do?” and nobody answered.

The others laughed a little louder at Tenzin's jokes than they needed to. I couldn't tell whether they liked Tenzin or just feared the cold shoulder. When Tenzin asked, “Who's coming to my birthday?” four hands shot up quickly. Ria's hand went up last, and only halfway.

qa.q: What happened to Ria the next week?
qa.a: Tenzin stopped looking at Ria at all, and Ria kept asking, “What did I do?” while nobody answered.

qa.q: What might have made the others laugh louder than they needed to?
qa.a: They may have feared losing Tenzin's favour, so a louder laugh was a way of proving loyalty, though Vaibhav cannot be sure.

qa.q: What could Vaibhav do the next time Ria asks what Ria did?
qa.a: Vaibhav could answer honestly that Ria did nothing wrong and invite Ria to sit at another table.

qa.q: What might it feel like for Ria to raise a hand only halfway for the birthday?
qa.a: Ria probably felt anxious and unsure whether to hope, wanting to belong again but afraid of being turned down.

grounding: A peer watches the group's leader decide who is in favour each week, keeping everyone anxious and obedient.

passage:
Monday: At lunch, Zainab watched Thomas, the group's leader, call Rohit over. “Sit here, bro.” Rohit beamed. Everyone moved up for him.
Wednesday: Rohit said something about a film Thomas didn't like. Thomas turned his back. By the afternoon, nobody sat next to Rohit. Nobody said why. The whole group just followed Thomas's cue.
Friday: Rohit brought samosas for everyone and laughed too hard at Thomas's jokes. Thomas let him sit at the end. The rest of the group laughed nervously too, watching Thomas's face.
Zainab ate her lunch quietly. She'd been at the end once. She knew how it felt, and she was careful never to disagree with Thomas either.

qa.q: What did Rohit bring on Friday?
qa.a: He brought samosas for everyone.

qa.q: What was Zainab feeling as she watched?
qa.a: She felt anxious and wary, careful never to disagree with Thomas because she'd been out of favour once.

qa.q: What could Zainab do to loosen Thomas's control?
qa.a: She could sit with Rohit when he's frozen out, or find one other friend who also feels uneasy, so the group isn't run by one person's mood.

qa.q: How might Rohit have felt on Wednesday afternoon?
qa.a: Rohit likely felt confused and anxious, shut out without knowing why.

grounding: Shows a peer watching a group leader decide who is in favour each week, keeping everyone anxious and obedient.

passage:
Jomon, you asked why I don't like groups with one boss. Let me tell you. This is your Rashmi aunty, and this is from Class 9.
Our group had a leader, Sheela. Every Monday, she decided who was “in”. If she liked your bag, you were in. If you talked to the wrong girl, you were out, and nobody would sit with you till she said so.
I watched it happen to my friend Mini. For a whole week, Sheela ignored her, and so did everyone. Even me. I was scared I'd be next.
We all behaved perfectly for Sheela. We laughed at her jokes. We gave her our best pens. We were so busy watching her face, we forgot to be friends with each other.
I never stood up to her. That's what I remember most.

qa.q: Who decided who was "in" every Monday?
qa.a: Sheela did.

qa.q: How did young Rashmi feel when Mini was frozen out?
qa.a: She felt scared and anxious that she'd be next, so she ignored Mini too.

qa.q: At what point in the story could young Rashmi have made a different choice?
qa.a: During Mini's week of being ignored, she could have kept sitting with Mini, even if it risked Sheela's favour.

qa.q: How might Mini have felt that week?
qa.a: She probably felt hurt and alone, with even her friend Rashmi ignoring her.

grounding: An elder recalls watching a group leader decide who was in favour each week, keeping everyone fearful and obedient, herself included.

passage:
Rain poured on the sports camp, and the bus back to school was leaving in ten minutes. Neil, captain of everything, stood at the bus door, deciding who sat at the back with him.
“Farhan, back. Mehul, back. Aman... no, front today.”
Aman's face fell. Last week he'd been at the back every day. Nobody asked Neil why. Everyone just moved where he pointed.
Charu, dripping at the end of the queue, watched them all glance at Neil's face as they passed him, checking. She'd been sent to the front once, for laughing at the wrong joke.
Aman sat alone in the second row, looking out at the rain. Charu hesitated, then sat next to him. From the back, she heard Neil laugh. She didn't turn round.

qa.q: How long before the bus was leaving?
qa.a: It was leaving in ten minutes.

qa.q: What was Charu feeling as she watched everyone check Neil's face?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and a bit afraid, remembering being sent to the front once for laughing at the wrong joke.

qa.q: What did Charu do that weakened Neil's control a little?
qa.a: She sat with Aman, so he wasn't alone, showing that Neil's choices didn't have to decide everyone's.

qa.q: How might Aman have felt being sent to the front?
qa.a: He likely felt hurt and confused, dropped from the back without any reason.

grounding: Shows a peer watching a group leader decide who sits where, keeping everyone anxious, and quietly sitting with the one left out.

passage:
Every Monday, Varun could tell who was in favour just by watching Pranav's bench in the Class 10 corridor of their Hyderabad school. This week it was Kabir: Pranav shared his earphones with him and laughed at every joke. Last week it had been Rishi. Now Rishi stood at the edge, laughing a beat too late.
Nobody argued with Pranav. When he called the new cricket captain "a nobody", three boys agreed within seconds, though one of them had voted for that captain.
Varun had been in favour once, in Class 8. He remembered waiting for Pranav's reply to every message.
On Thursday Pranav said, "Rishi's getting so annoying, na?" Rishi went pale. Everyone looked at their shoes. Varun heard himself say, "He's fine, Pranav," and then his heart was pounding.

qa.q: Who was in favour with Pranav this week?
qa.a: Kabir was in favour this week.

qa.q: What was Varun feeling after saying "He's fine, Pranav"?
qa.a: Varun's heart was pounding; he felt scared of losing his place, yet steadier for finally speaking.

qa.q: What could the boys do so Pranav's moods stop ruling the group?
qa.a: Back each other up like Varun did, and make plans or opinions without waiting for Pranav's approval.

qa.q: What is it like for Rishi now that he is out of favour?
qa.a: Rishi feels anxious and unsure, laughing a beat too late and going pale when Pranav turns on him.

grounding: Shows a peer watching a group leader decide who is in favour each week, keeping everyone anxious and obedient.
